Fonts and Troubleshooting

Source: vignettes/font-installation-troubleshooting.Rmd
font-installation-troubleshooting.Rmd

Most users should not install fonts manually. docdesigner ships the text and code fonts used by its built-in PDF styles.

What the Package Bundles

The bundled fonts live in inst/fonts/ and are used automatically by docdesigner::pdf and docdesigner::snapshot.

Bundled font families:

  • Source Serif 4
  • EB Garamond
  • XITS
  • Fira Code

A style may declare additional families under fonts.<Family> and ship the face files in its own assets/fonts/ directory. Matching math fonts are optional; when one is unavailable, the engine default is used instead of treating it as a render failure.

Check Your Setup

Run:

docdesigner::designer_check()

The check reports:

  • bundled template path
  • bundled fonts path
  • bundled CSL path
  • style bundle availability
  • rmarkdown
  • Pandoc
  • common LaTeX engines

Local Editable Copies

Most projects should use bundled assets. If you deliberately keep local editable copies, refresh them with:

docdesigner::designer_update_templates()

This updates:

  • docdesignertemplate.tex
  • default.csl
  • fonts/
  • sets/

To pull the latest assets from GitHub:

docdesigner::designer_update_templates(source = "github", branch = "main")

Common Problems

If rmarkdown is missing, install it before rendering:

install.packages("rmarkdown")

If Pandoc is missing, install RStudio, Quarto, or Pandoc directly and confirm that rmarkdown::pandoc_available() returns TRUE.

If a LaTeX engine is missing, install a TeX distribution such as TinyTeX, MiKTeX, or TeX Live. Then rerun:

docdesigner::designer_check()

If a project uses local assets and fonts are stale, run:

docdesigner::designer_update_templates(overwrite = TRUE)
